questions.prompt: In Anthropic's prompt chaining, what is a "gate"?

options.text: A paid tier of the model that unlocks longer outputs after you have made a payment
options.explanation: A gate is a check inside a chain. It has nothing to do with pricing.

options.text: A programmatic check on a middle step, to confirm the process is still on track
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic adds these checks on intermediate steps so a chain does not carry an error forward.

options.text: The final file that the agent hands to the client once every earlier step has passed
options.explanation: The gate sits between steps, not at the end.

questions.prompt: In Runway's Multi-Shot Video custom mode, what must the per-shot durations do?

options.text: They must each be 8 seconds long, whatever the total
options.explanation: Runway sets no 8-second rule for shots. The durations must add up to the total.

options.text: They can be any length, because the recipe trims the end
options.explanation: Runway says to make sure the durations add up to the total duration.

options.text: They must add up to the total duration of the video
options.explanation: Right. Runway says that in custom mode each shot's duration must add up to the total duration.

questions.prompt: How does OpenAI's orchestration guide say to treat each specialist agent?

options.text: Give each specialist a narrow job, and begin with just one agent whenever you can
options.explanation: Right. The guide says to keep each specialist's job narrow and to begin with a single agent.

options.text: Give each specialist the whole project, so that any of them can finish the job alone
options.explanation: The guide advises a narrow job for each specialist, not the whole project.

options.text: Add a new specialist for every step, so that every step has its own agent from day one
options.explanation: The guide says to start with one agent and add specialists only when the contract changes.
